coverage: Opening and all four parts in both English editions: every named individual and the historically identifiable opening Pope/Czar. Political classes, movements and institutions are not invented personal characters.

entities.name: Pope Pius IX
entities.body: The pope at the time of the Manifesto’s publication in 1848.

entities.name: Nicholas I
entities.body: The Russian emperor referred to as the Czar in the opening.

entities.name: Klemens von Metternich
entities.body: The Austrian statesman associated with the conservative European order.

entities.name: François Guizot
entities.body: The French statesman and historian prominent under the July Monarchy.

entities.name: Jean Charles Léonard de Sismondi
entities.body: The economist and critic of industrial capitalism discussed under petty-bourgeois socialism.

entities.name: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
entities.body: The French socialist thinker whose Philosophy of Poverty is cited.

entities.name: Gracchus Babeuf
entities.body: The French revolutionary associated with radical economic equality.

entities.name: Henri de Saint-Simon
entities.body: The French social thinker grouped here with Fourier and Owen.

entities.name: Charles Fourier
entities.body: The French socialist thinker known for planned cooperative communities.

entities.name: Robert Owen
entities.body: The social reformer associated with cooperative communities and improved working conditions.
